To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
happy (vs. unhappy) people are better at self-control tasks when they have an accessible self-improvement (vs. mood management) goal.

happy (vs. sad) people are more likely to engage in self-control behaviors if they have a self-improving goal in mind, but are less likely to engage in such behaviors if they have mood management goal in mind.

people in a positive mood (a) are more likely to engage in self-control when the goal of the task is self-improvement (vs. when the goal is mood management), but (b) are less likely to engage in a self-control task that is incompatible with the goal of mood management (e.g., seeking negative feedback).
In summary, our research is concerned with
how mood affects self-regulation, but we propose that the effects are moderated by the accessibility of goals.
how the effects of mood on self-regulatory success depend on the accessibility of a goal.
the question of how people's moods influence their self-control success.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mood affects self-control by influencing whether people choose to engage in self-control tasks that are consistent with their accessible goals.
mood affects self-control success, but only when the person is motivated to improve (vs. manage) her mood.
mood influences self-control success by activating or de-activating an accessible goal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mood can influence self-control, but it does so in an indirect way, by affecting the accessibility of goals.
mood can be better or be merry, depending on what you want to achieve.
people in good mood are more likely to engage in self-control behaviors when the behaviors further their goals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mood does not affect self-control success in a simple way, but rather depends on a person’s goals.
mood affects self-control success in a goal-specific way.
the effects of positive mood on self-control depend on the person's goals.
